# quoted first, exactly as printed (his spelling, his capitals), and the
# description that follows is this edition's. Plain text, no brackets.

column2: “The Merry Friar carrieth Robin across the Water.” Friar Tuck, knee-deep in a reedy stream, carries Robin Hood across on his back, with a castle on the hill behind them.
A decorative banner lettered “Preface,” framed in leafy scrollwork with a small sun at the top.
A tailpiece in the shape of a downward triangle: inside a round frame, one hand reaches down to take another, above a river and a far-off town.
“Young Robin goes to the Shooting-Match.” Young Robin strides through a sunny wood with his bow over his shoulder; beside him, the title is lettered on a ribbon among the flowers.

“Robin Hood meeteth the tall Stranger on the Bridge.” The tall stranger, soon to be Little John, stands on the log bridge leaning on his staff, laughing down at Robin, who has been knocked into the stream among the lily pads.
A bundle of arrows and a broken bow tied up with a ribbon lettered “Dieu et mon droit,” French for “God and my right,” the motto of the kings of England, with daffodils.

“Robin and the Tinker at the Blue Boar Inn.” Outside the inn, under its sign, Robin sits on a bench grinning while the Tinker sprawls on the cobbles beside his staff and his mug, with townsfolk watching.
“The Sheriff of Nottingham plotting against Robin sends a messinger to Lincoln.” A rider gallops past a signpost marked “To Lincoln,” across open country with a windmill on the skyline.
“The Sheriff of Nottingham cometh before the King at London.” The Sheriff bows low before King Henry and Queen Eleanor, who sit enthroned among their courtiers in a garden.

“The Aged Palmer gives Young David of Doncaster news of Will Stutely.” Outside the town walls, an old pilgrim with a long beard, a staff and a rosary talks to young David, who stands with his hand on his hip.
A tailpiece of curling leaves around a man in armor grappling with another, with the initials H. P. below.
“Robin turns butcher and sells his meat in Nottingham.” At his market stall, Robin leans across the table to give a pretty young woman a kiss, while a crowd of townswomen behind her laugh.
“Robin buys the Butcher's meat.” On a country road, Robin talks with the young butcher beside his covered cart and horse.

“Little John overcomes Eric o' Lincoln.” On a wooden platform at the fair, Little John stands with his staff over Eric, who lies flat on his back with his hat knocked off, while people watch from the benches.
“The Mighty Fight betwixt Little John and the Cook.” In the Sheriff's kitchen, Little John and the Cook lunge at each other with swords, with a tangle of cloth on the floor between them.
“The stout bout between Little John and Arthur a Bland.” In a forest clearing, Little John and the Tanner swing their long quarterstaffs at each other.
“Little John knoweth not which Road to take.” Little John stands at a crossroads scratching his head, under signs pointing to Ancaster and to the Blue Boar, with the sun rising behind him.
“Merry Robin stops a Stranger in Scarlet.” On the highway, Robin, seen from behind with his staff, blocks the way of an elegant young man in fancy clothes who is calmly smelling a rose.
“The Four Yeomen have Merry Sport with a Stout Miller.” The yeomen and the Miller bend low together over his open sack of flour, all peering in.
A tailpiece of sheaves of wheat around a round frame in which a hand holds a staff over a cloud of flour.
“Allan a Dale lieth beside the Fountain.” A young man lies face down on the grass beside a still pool under an overhanging tree.
“Allan a Dale tells his Story.” A decorative banner with the title, framed by scrollwork and figures of listening yeomen.
“The Merry Friar sings a goodly Song.” A stout friar sits under the willows by the water with his legs stretched out, holding up a flask and singing with his mouth wide open.

“Robin Hood steps betwixt Sir Stephen and his Bride.” In the church, Robin, in his tall feathered minstrel's hat, stands between the old knight and the young bride, while the Bishop in his tall miter looks on.
A tailpiece of a round frame among roses and crossed arrows, showing the profiles of a young man and a young woman side by side under two stars.
“Merry Robin stops a Sorrowful Knight.” Robin, staff in hand, smiles up at a knight in a long robe riding a big horse whose blanket is embroidered with pictures.
“The young Knight of the Lea overcometh the Knight of Lancaster.” A jousting scene: one armored knight on a decorated horse bears down on another who is falling, with shields hanging on a tree.
“Sir Richard pleadeth before the Prior of Emmet.” Sir Richard kneels on the stone floor of the dining hall before the fat Prior, who lounges in a great chair with a goblet, among his guests.
“The Covetous Prior.” Inside a round frame held up by two winged sea serpents, the Prior sits counting his money at a table.

“Little John in ye guise of a Friar stops three Lasses.” Little John, dressed as a friar, stands with his hands on his hips in front of three young women with baskets of eggs, under a sign for Tuxford.
“Little John journeys in holy Company.” Little John in a friar's robe walks along a road between two monks on horseback, with men on foot far down the road.
“Merry Robin clad as a Beggar stops the Corn Engrosser by the Cross nigh Ollerton.” Robin in a beggar's rags and a tall hat grabs the bridle of a thin, sour-faced rider by a wayside cross.
A tailpiece shaped like a downward triangle, with a worn old shoe inside a round frame ringed with beads.
“Allan a Dale singeth before our good Queen Eleanor.” Allan sits playing his harp in the palace, while Queen Eleanor, her ladies and Robin's yeomen sit and listen.
“Young Richard Partington cometh to seek Merry Robin Hood.” A page gallops past a signpost marked “To Sherwood,” with a town and a castle behind him.
“Stout Robin hath a narrow escape.” Robin kneels to drink at a stream as one arrow flies just past his head and another splashes into the water beside his hand.
A tailpiece of curling leaves around an archer in a feathered cap drawing his bow, beneath a shield with a lion.
“Robin Hood slayeth Guy of Gisbourne.” Robin stands under a tree, wiping his sword, over the body of Guy of Gisbourne, who lies face down in his horsehide cloak.
“Robin and Little John go their ways in search of Adventure.” Robin and Little John part beneath a tree and set off along two different roads, their staffs on their shoulders.
“Merry Robin hath the worst of a Bargain.” Robin lies flat on the grass after the blow, while the tall hooded friar who struck him, King Richard in disguise, stands over him and the band watches.
A tailpiece with the Latin motto “Cucullus non facit monachum,” “the hood does not make the monk”: a tall man in a monk's habit stands beneath a shining crown, and a yeoman kneels before him.

“Robin shooteth his last Shaft.” Robin, propped in bed in the nunnery and held by Little John, draws his bow at the open window. Above, the name AZRAEL, the angel of death, is lettered across the top.
“So ye Great Reaper reapeth among the Flowers.” A hooded figure bends to cut flowers with a sickle under a dark sky. (“Ye” is an old way of printing “the.”)
The closing ornament: a banner lettered “Finis,” Latin for “the end,” between two small seated archers, above a pointed pattern of black scrollwork.
